title: Dg resolution-square projection and its relative localization
statement:
Use cochain complexes and quasi-isomorphisms as in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and dg categories, quasi-equivalences and derived dg functor categories as in [lem-coef-dg-quasifunctor-invariance], in sufficiently large fixed universes. Let $\mathcal A$ be a dg category over $\mathbf Z$, and $\mathcal D,\mathcal E$ full dg subcategories. Let $S$ be a set of closed degree-zero arrows $s:e_s\to d_s$ with $e_s\in\mathcal E$ and $d_s\in\mathcal D$. Assume every object of $\mathcal D$ equals some $d_s$, and for every $s,t\in S$ postcomposition induces a degreewise surjective quasi-isomorphism
$$\mathcal A(e_s,e_t)\longrightarrow\mathcal A(e_s,d_t).$$
Define $\mathcal R$ to have objects $S$ and morphism complexes
$$\mathcal R(s,t)=\mathcal A(e_s,e_t)\times_{\mathcal A(e_s,d_t)}\mathcal A(d_s,d_t),$$
with the two maps postcomposition by $t$ and precomposition by $s$, differential and composition componentwise. Let $\pi:\mathcal R\to\mathcal D$ send $s$ to $d_s$ and a square $(a,b)$ to $b$. Then $\pi$ is surjective on objects and a degreewise surjective quasi-isomorphism on every morphism complex. Every closed degree-zero arrow between the projected objects lifts to a closed degree-zero square. In particular $\pi$ is a quasi-equivalence.

For any collection $W$ of closed degree-zero arrows of $\mathcal D$, put $W_{\mathcal R}=\{u:\pi(u)\in W\}$. The induced functor of enriched localizations in [lem-coef-enhanced-localization-universal]
$$\mathcal R[W_{\mathcal R}^{-1}]\longrightarrow\mathcal D[W^{-1}]$$
is an equivalence, including its induced functor and transformation objects and coherent diagram categories. The dual assertion holds for arrows $s:d_s\to e_s$ if every $d\in\mathcal D$ occurs and precomposition gives degreewise surjective quasi-isomorphisms $\mathcal A(e_s,e_t)\to\mathcal A(d_s,e_t)$: use morphism complexes $\mathcal A(d_s,d_t)\times_{\mathcal A(d_s,e_t)}\mathcal A(e_s,e_t)$ and projection to the $\mathcal D$ component.
